note: Bottomland forest along an unchannelized stretch of Yellow Creek, beside Swan Lake National Wildlife Refuge. Two designated camping areas on Hog Ridge Avenue, 400 m apart with the road's creek bridge between them. The northern one is a small gravel lot at the trailhead, a rig or two at most; the southern one is only a roadside pull-off under the trees. No pads, tables, toilets or water. Yellow Creek bends within 50 m of the northern lot behind timber. The bottoms flood; the suspension footbridge on the trail is out of service (flood damage). --Claude
summary: Confirmed: two designated camping areas (map symbols + GIS points), each beside one of the area's two parking spots on Hog Ridge Avenue, 390 m apart - stays as designated points at lots. Neither is built. The north lot is the real one; the pin is in the woods by the south pull-off - move proposed. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. Not waterfront stands (creek lead reported). Phone matches. No split.
flags: DESIGNATED POINTS (lot rule - STAYS): page lists 'Individual Campsites'; brochure: 'Camping is permitted in designated areas and is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' The 8/19/2024 map legend has 'Primitive Camping' and draws two symbols, each directly under a Parking Lot symbol on the west edge by Hog Ridge Avenue. GIS layer 27: two 'Primitive Camping Area' points, 39.58494,-93.23561 (north) and 39.58144,-93.23583 (south, the stored pin); layer 26: two lots, 39.58550,-93.23552 and 39.58183,-93.23615.

WHAT IS ON THE GROUND - NORTH: a gravel lot about 15 x 25 m on a short gravel stub east of Hog Ridge Avenue, at the head of the trail to the suspension bridge; it opens onto a mown cleared strip about 30 m wide that runs north-south through the forest (gates or barriers across it). The GIS camping point is 60 m south of the lot at the west edge of that strip, with no pad or track. Nothing built.

WHAT IS ON THE GROUND - SOUTH (the pin): no real lot - a gravel widening about 8 x 8 m on the east shoulder of Hog Ridge Avenue under the trees (where the GIS lot point is); the GIS camping point is 45 m south-east of it in standing timber beside the same cleared strip. Nothing built, nothing drivable at the point.

PIN MOVE (about 440 m): stored 39.58144,-93.23583 (south GIS camping point, in the woods) -> proposed 39.58542,-93.23553, the gravel of the north lot. The north lot is the clear main spot: the only place with room to park a motorhome off the road, and the first one reached from Sumner without crossing the creek bridge.
NO SPLIT: the two points are 390 m apart on the same road.

ACCESS: Hog Ridge Avenue is a gravel county road ('Non-MDC Road' on the map). From Sumner (the page's directions) the north lot comes first. Between the two spots the road crosses Yellow Creek on a raised single-lane bridge about 30 m long (casts a shadow on the water on imagery - a real bridge, not a slab); I could not read any posted weight limit for it. The map legend's 'Low Water Bridge' symbol is drawn only at the far east end of the hiking trail, not on the road. Brochure: 'Motor vehicles are restricted to graveled roadways and parking areas.' No 4WD wording.

NOTICES on the page today: 'The suspension footbridge over yellow creek has been damaged by repeated flooding and is no longer safe for foot travel. Bridge will be taken out of service and repaired at a later date.' and 'Yellow Creek Conservation Area is now open to Waterfowl hunting per statewide regulations'. Neither closes the camping; the footbridge line is in the note. The 'bottoms flood' wording rests on that notice and the page's 'historic Yellow Creek floods'.

FIRES: brochure 'Unattended camp or warming fires are prohibited. All fires may be restricted during times of extreme fire danger.' No fire ban. No horse camp (brochure: equestrian use only on roads open to vehicles).

WATERFRONT LEAD - NOT CHANGED, reads as not waterfront: Yellow Creek (about 12-15 m wide here, so 'creekside' vocabulary) bends about 50 m east of the north lot and about 50 m west of it across the road; standing bottomland timber lies between the lot and the water on both sides, with no open ground to the bank. The south pull-off is about 55 m from the creek, also through timber. No page or photo claims a view.
PHONE: stored 660-646-6122 matches the page's 'For more information call (660) 646-6122' (brochure: Chillicothe Office 660/646-6122).
Nothing else in the database within 5 km.
